maya: Quick sync — we need a compact edge-case checklist for generation resilience to include in the PRD. focus: streaming, truncation, token limits, retries. short bullet-style examples please.
alex (eng-runtime): +1. should cover deterministic vs nondeterministic truncation behavior and resume semantics.
sam (ml infra): Also call out kv-cache invalidation on retries and when to invalidate vs reuse.
helen (product): Customers (finance/reg) asked for clear acceptance criteria: what counts as a successful resume vs acceptable fallback.
maya: Draft outline idea: 1) streaming cutoffs: graceful close vs send partial, 2) resume token protocol, 3) retry idempotency contract, 4) token-limit errors and suggestions, 5) metrics/alerts. anyone add quick examples?
alex (eng-runtime): Example streaming cutoff states: 
- server-initiated cutoff (seq_len cap) -> emit END_STREAM event + truncated flag.
- client disconnect -> allow resume window 60s with resume_id.
- rate-limited preemption -> best-effort partial + X-RETRY-ABLE header.
Add acceptance: truncated responses must include `truncated:true` and `prompt_truncation_reason`.
sam (ml infra): For resume protocol: resume_id tied to session + model_variant + kv_cache_version. On resume, client provides resume_id and last_ack_token_index. Server verifies kv_cache_version match else reject with 409 and fallback suggestion.
helen (product): Acceptance criteria bullets: 
- Resume success rate >= 98% in staged tests for <60s disconnects.
- If resume fails, fallback to short-form regenerate within 300ms median failover latency.
- Truncation must be explicit in payload (flag + human-readable reason).
maya: Token-limit handling: differentiate between prompt-truncation (client-side guidance) vs generation cutoff (model hit max output tokens). Include clear error codes: 413_PROMPT_TOO_LONG, 429_OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE, 420_SEQ_OVERFLOW.
alex (eng-runtime): Retries: only safe when request is idempotent or has deterministic resume markers. For non-idempotent chat streams, allow 'replay-from' semantics: client supplies last_received_token_id and dedupe on server up to N tokens. Replays should be capped to 256 tokens.
sam (ml infra): Note about KV cache: don't accept resume if server-side cache eviction happened (eviction window differs by backend). Signal `resume_unavailable` + preferred fallback.
helen (product): Edge cases to call out in PRD section: 
- multi-device resume (same session from different client)
- model variant fallback during resume (e.g., quantized fallback) -> must be explicitly allowed by customer config
- partial billing: how we bill for truncated/failed attempts
maya: Quick QA checklist for launch: 
- unit tests for resume idempotency and 409 flows
- e2e inject disconnects at various points (0-5s, 5-60s, 60-600s)
- chaos test with KV eviction + resume attempts
- verify metrics: resume_success_rate, truncated_rate, retry_fallback_latency

alex (eng-runtime): Impl notes: include header `X-Resume-ID` and streaming control frames: `TRUNC`, `END`, `RESUME_OK`, `RESUME_FAIL`. Keep frame format backwards-compatible.

helen (product): Can we get small language in marketing/FAQ about "what happens when a stream cuts off"? want to avoid legal/reg confusion.

maya: Thanks all — I'll turn this into a short PRD appendix and put acceptance criteria into the launch checklist. tagging @ops-bot to create a follow-up ticket. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Created ticket INF-6234: "Gen API: Resume + Truncation acceptance tests" assigned to eng-runtime.

alex (eng-runtime): I'll take INF-6234, will post short RFC draft later today with flow diagrams and sample payloads.

maya: Perfect. closing thread for now — will attach doc link when ready.
